# AO3. Google Ad Grants Eligibility and Organizational Readiness (Brian Vuong)

## Current Evidence Synthesis

Research shows that digital-marketing readiness requires more than access to a website, analytics platform, or advertising account. Effective implementation also depends on website quality, staff expertise, leadership support, campaign ownership, conversion tracking, and the ability to apply analytics to decisions [@yoon2024; @xiao2026; @herradaLores2022; @olinski2026]. Technology access alone does not guarantee stronger visibility or performance when an organization lacks the capacity to interpret and use its data [@kovalenkoKuzmenko2020]. Paid search also interacts with SEO, competition, website quality, and changing search conditions, while metrics such as clicks and traffic provide limited value unless connected to meaningful audience actions [@li2026; @vollrathVillegas2022]. Therefore, Wellness Ranch should be evaluated through a multidimensional readiness assessment rather than a basic eligibility checklist. The Technology-Organization-Environment framework will provide the primary structure, while the Customer Decision Journey and a website and analytics audit will support the evaluation of user behavior and conversions. Final readiness criteria will be established after reviewing Google requirements, client information, and system access.

## Current Framework Decision

The current proposed approach uses the Technology-Organization-Environment framework as the primary model. The Customer Decision Journey serves as a supplementary framework for connecting website and campaign activity to meaningful audience actions and conversions. A structured readiness matrix will translate the frameworks and current Google requirements into operational assessment criteria. This approach remains preliminary pending client interviews, system access, and faculty-lead feedback.

## Model-Comparison Table

| Approach / Model | What It Explains | Evidence For / Against | Data / Assumptions | Fit with AO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Technology-Organization-Environment | Explains readiness through technological capacity, organizational capacity, and external requirements | Supported by nonprofit digital-adoption evidence; may be too broad without operational criteria | Requires website, organizational, account, and environmental information | Strong primary fit |
| Customer Decision Journey | Connects audience needs, journey stages, website behavior, and meaningful conversions | Helps avoid analytics myopia; does not fully assess organizational eligibility or capacity | Requires defined audiences, desired actions, and measurable journey stages | Strong supplementary fit |
| Website and analytics audit | Evaluates technical website quality, landing pages, events, funnels, and conversions | Produces practical evidence but does not independently explain organizational sustainability | Requires Wix, GA4, Search Console, and donation-process access | Strong diagnostic fit but insufficient alone |
| Combined TOE, Customer Decision Journey, and readiness matrix | Integrates eligibility, technology, organizational capacity, user behavior, measurement, and compliance | Comprehensive and suitable for a single-client assessment; requires clearly justified scoring criteria | Requires multiple data sources and transparent classification rules | Most defensible current approach |

## Unresolved Questions

- Does Wellness Ranch meet all current Google Ad Grants eligibility requirements?
- What documentation and Google for Nonprofits access are available?
- Which website actions should be treated as meaningful conversions?
- Are the necessary GA4 events configured and tested?
- Who will manage the campaigns after the capstone project concludes?
- What evidence should determine whether an area is Ready, Partially Ready, or Not Ready?
- Should AO3 retain its current wording or be clarified after the readiness assessment?

## Guidance Requested from the Faculty Lead

- Is the combined TOE and Customer Decision Journey approach appropriately scoped for AO3?
- Is a three-level readiness matrix sufficiently defensible for this client-consulting project?
- Should the team retain the original AO wording while treating the readiness criteria as preliminary?
- Are additional academic frameworks or data sources needed before the method is finalized?
